messages.content: Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.  Discuss how likely the predictions below are.  • Privacy will become a thing of the past. • By the early 2030s, we will be able to copy human consciousness to a computer. • Wireless Internet connection will be available anywhere on our planet. • All forms of transport will eventually become electric. • The effects of climate change will be irreversible. • Physical money (coins and notes) won't exist anymore. • Scientists will unlock the genetic secrets that could allow us to live for centuries, maybe forever.

message.content:
Privacy will likely shrink in online spaces, but complete disappearance is improbable because encryption, regulation, and behavior can still protect personal information. Privacy
Consciousness copying by the early 2030s is extremely unlikely because we lack a map of subjective experience, and digital replication would face unresolved neuroscience and ethics. Consciousness
Wireless coverage will likely expand to almost every place, but total global availability is moderate because terrain, power, demand, and policy create gaps. Wireless
Transport electrification will likely become dominant over time, but total electrification of every mode is less certain because aviation, shipping, and niche uses may remain hard to power fully electrically. Transport
Effects of climate change will likely include irreversible losses, especially at high warming, because some systems cross tipping points and accumulate damage. Effects
Money in physical form will likely decline, but complete global disappearance is less likely because cash remains useful for resilience, privacy, and inclusion. Money
Longevity science will likely extend healthy human life, but unlocking secrets for centuries or immortality is very unlikely because aging involves many interacting systems. Longevity
